tracks.display_name_ar: لائحة نقل البيانات الشخصية إلى خارج المملكة
tracks.display_name_en: Regulation on Transfer of Personal Data Outside the Kingdom
tracks.notes: Regulation on Transfer of Personal Data Outside the Kingdom «لائحة نقل البيانات الشخصية إلى خارج المملكة» — SDAIA President Decision No. (1840), dated 27/2/1446H, issued pursuant to Article (29) of the Personal Data Protection Law (M/19). Discovered via a targeted, precision-requested deep-dive scan for NCA/SDAIA binding instruments not yet in this corpus. **9 records, ALL اصلية**, flat structure (no أبواب/فصول). Its legislative basis (PDPL Article 29, sub-paragraph (د) of paragraph (1), paragraphs (ب)/(ج) of paragraph (2), and paragraph (4)) was independently re-verified by reading the article's own already-ingested text in this corpus (sources/pdpl/verified) rather than trusting the initial research lead. **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_1_PRIMARY_MULTI_SOURCE** — laws.boe.gov.sa unreachable this pass (TCP reset); PRIMARY reached via TWO INDEPENDENT official government sources in full agreement: SDAIA's own live portal (dgp.sdaia.gov.sa) and the Umm al-Qura Official Gazette (uqn.gov.sa), the latter additionally supplying the decree number/date the SDAIA portal itself omits. A structurally distinct predecessor regulation (same general subject, different title without the word 'إلى', 10 articles across 4 chapters) was independently confirmed to exist via its own Umm al-Qura gazette record (published 1445-2-22H/07-09-2023G) — but neither published text (old or new) contains an explicit repeal/supersession clause, and the predecessor's own promulgating decree number could not be independently confirmed this pass (a single unconfirmed WebSearch-surfaced candidate is disclosed but NOT relied upon). Supersession of the 2023 predecessor by this 2024 regulation is therefore reported as a **STRONG INFERENCE** (same subject/issuer, irreconcilable structural conflict between the two regimes, and multiple independent press/legal-aggregator sources describing the new regulation as an 'update' to prior regulations) — NOT an asserted fact. That predecessor is not itself a tracked instrument in this corpus, so no supersession-graph edge is added regardless of the confidence level. Arabic governs; not legal advice.
tracks.source_authority: Decision of the President of the Saudi Data and AI Authority (SDAIA) No. (1840), dated 27/2/1446H, issued pursuant to Article (29) of the Personal Data Protection Law (Royal Decree M/19, 9/2/1443H). Published in Umm al-Qura Official Gazette, 28/2/1446H (1 September 2024G). laws.boe.gov.sa unreachable this pass (TCP connection reset). PRIMARY x2 independent official government sources — SDAIA's own live portal (dgp.sdaia.gov.sa) and the Umm al-Qura Official Gazette (uqn.gov.sa) — both fetched directly (HTTP 200) and matching verbatim; SECONDARY aunklaw.com (full verbatim match) and LexisMiddleEast (confirms 'Version 2.0' labeling).

tracks.display_name_ar: الترتيبات التنظيمية للهيئة السعودية للبيانات والذكاء الاصطناعي
tracks.display_name_en: Organizational Arrangements of the Saudi Data and AI Authority (SDAIA)
tracks.notes: Organizational Arrangements of the Saudi Data and AI Authority «الترتيبات التنظيمية للهيئة السعودية للبيانات والذكاء الاصطناعي» — Council of Ministers Resolution No. (292), dated 27/4/1441H, amended by Resolution No. (195), 15/3/1444H. Discovered via the same targeted NCA/SDAIA deep-dive scan as pdpl_cross_border_transfer_regulation. **16 records: 15 اصلية / 1 معدلة (بند خامساً, board formation)**, flat structure of sixteen ordinal بند divisions (أولاً-سادس عشر) — like cybersecurity_authority_enablers, NOT divided into numbered مواد. **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_2** — no laws.boe.gov.sa lawId page located this pass (targeted site-restricted search surfaced only unrelated BOE-catalogued laws referencing SDAIA in passing). PRIMARY SDAIA's own official site PDF, whose direct fetch fails domain-wide in this sandbox (connection reset) — retrieved instead via the r.jina.ai reader-proxy. The proxy's extraction has a CONFIRMED, disclosed systematic character-order artifact (lam+alif-form bigrams render reversed, e.g. 'الاعتبارية' as 'االعتبارية') — independently confirmed against qistas.com's own clean preview of the first three بنود and corrected via disclosed, cross-validated word-level reconstruction, NOT pixel-level OCR (the PDF's raw bytes could not be obtained this pass: direct fetch, a Wayback replay, and a CORS proxy all failed). SECONDARY cross-verification from qistas.com, lexismiddleeast.com (confirms the Resolution 195 amendment targets specifically بند خامساً), almirkaz.com, and qanoniah.com (existence/citation only, both paywalled beyond preview). **CONFIRMED, INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED (via the Saudi Press Agency's own text of founding Royal Order A/471)**: the pre-existing National Information Center (Royal Order A/293/1438H, CoM Resolution 495/1439H) was organizationally absorbed under SDAIA without an explicit repeal of its own founding instrument — a genuine NEGATIVE finding, disclosed rather than silently omitted. This instrument's final بند (سادس عشر) contains only a publication/effective-date clause with NO repeal language of any kind, and carries no violations/penalties clause anywhere. The amendment attribution for بند خامساً rests solely on a secondary aggregator's (LexisMiddleEast) own indexing metadata, not an independently-obtained pre/post-amendment textual diff — disclosed as a limited-confidence attribution. Arabic governs; not legal advice.

Amended by Council of Ministers Resolution No. (195), dated 15/3/1444H. laws.boe.gov.sa: no dedicated lawId page located this pass despite a targeted search. tracks.display_name_en: Implementing Regulation of the Trade Names Law
tracks.notes: Implementing Regulation of the Trade Names Law «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام الأسماء التجارية» — issued under clause 'Second' (ثانيا) of Ministry of Commerce Decision No. (288), dated 20 Ramadan 1446H (20 March 2025G), pursuant to Article 22 of the Trade Names Law (Royal Decree M/83, 19/3/1446H). **19 records, ALL اصلية** (18 articles + Annex (1), fee schedule), flat structure with no أبواب/فصول. **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_3** — no laws.boe.gov.sa lawId page located for this 2025 ministerial regulation; uqn.gov.sa is an unreadable Vue.js SPA; mc.gov.sa's own Regulations-listing page failed to connect. PRIMARY qanoonsa.com (a private legal database that itself explicitly disclaims official-source status in its footer, relied upon only because every direct government channel was unreachable this pass), cross-verified via a byte-identical independent Wayback Machine snapshot and against ndmlaw.sa's verbatim law-firm quotations of Articles 6, 8, and 10; mc.gov.sa's own news bulletin independently confirms the decision number/date and joint effective date (metadata only, not full text). **Omnibus decision disambiguated**: Decision 288 approves FOUR distinct instruments in one signature — (i) the Commercial Register Law's own implementing regulation (a separate sibling track, commercial_register_regulation, built independently and not overlapping this track's text), (ii) THIS Regulation (clause 'Second', 18 articles + Annex 1), (iii) a transitional mechanism for correcting subsidiary commercial-register status (out of scope, not ingested), and (iv) controls for trade names registered before the new Law's effective date (out of scope, title only, not fetched or verified). An initial-research Hijri date of '30 Rabi al-Thani 1446H' was found to be incorrect and independently corrected via Hijri/Gregorian conversion to 20 Ramadan 1446H (signature) / 1 Shawwal 1446H (gazette publication). This Regulation's own Article 18 contains no explicit repeal clause naming its 1420H/2015 predecessor (Ministry of Commerce and Industry Decision No. 2015, 29 articles per WIPO Lex, not independently verified in full); supersession is inferred only from the repeal of the old base Trade Names Law itself. The Annex (1) fee table and the Article 15 violations table are preserved as flattened line-by-line strings per the source, including a disclosed inconsistent numeral format (one fine shown as '(10,000)' with a Latin thousands comma vs. others as '(5000)') and invisible RLM marks stripped as non-content formatting artifacts. A pre-enactment draft version was circulated for public consultation in January 2025 but was not compared against the final enacted text. Arabic governs; not legal advice.
tracks.source_authority: Ministry of Commerce Decision No. (288), dated 20 Ramadan 1446H (20 March 2025G), clause 'Second' (ثانيا) thereof, issued pursuant to Article 22 of the Trade Names Law (Royal Decree M/83, 19/3/1446H). Published in Umm al-Qura Official Gazette, Issue (5079), 30 March 2025G; effective 5 Shawwal 1446H (3 April 2025G). Decision 288 is a single omnibus instrument whose OTHER three clauses approve three separate instruments (the Commercial Register Law's own implementing regulation — a sibling track, commercial_register_regulation; a transitional subsidiary-register correction mechanism; and controls for trade names registered before the new Law's effective date) — none within this track's scope. laws.boe.gov.sa: no dedicated lawId page located for this 2025 ministerial regulation. uqn.gov.sa (Umm al-Qura's live portal): a Vue.js SPA whose direct fetch returns only unrendered template markup. PRIMARY qanoonsa.com (fetched directly, HTTP 200; explicitly disclaims official-source status in its own footer), cross-checked via an independent, byte-identical Wayback Machine snapshot of the same page and against ndmlaw.sa (law-firm commentary quoting Articles 6, 8, and 10 verbatim); mc.gov.sa's own news bulletin independently confirms Decision 288, Royal Decree M/83, and the joint effective date, though it supplies metadata only, not the full text.

tracks.display_name_en: Implementing Regulation of the Commercial Agencies Law
tracks.notes: Implementing Regulation of the Commercial Agencies Law «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام الوكالات التجارية» — Ministry of Commerce Resolution No. (1897), dated 24/5/1401H (30 March 1981G), issued under Article 3 of the Commercial Agencies Law (Royal Decree No. 11, 20/02/1382H). A new track, independent of this corpus's already-verified base-law track (commercial_agencies). **49 records: 21 اصلية / 1 معدلة / 27 مضافة** — 22 articles in the main body across five sections (General Provisions 1-5; Registration 6-15; De-registration 16-18; Violations/Penalties 19-21; Transitional 22), plus an independently-numbered 27-article Annex on maintenance/spare-parts/warranty obligations, matching the portal's own counters ('49 articles', '6 sections'). **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_2** — laws.boe.gov.sa has no dedicated lawId page for this ministerial-level Regulation (only for the base Law); PRIMARY is mc.gov.sa's own LIVE Regulations portal page, reached via the r.jina.ai reader-proxy after direct curl/WebFetch AND a Wayback Machine snapshot of the same URL both hit a BotDetect CAPTCHA challenge page. Not raised to TIER_1 because: only a SINGLE successful live fetch was obtained (a follow-up r.jina.ai attempt to re-fetch the same page, or to reach a third source, spa.gov.sa, was blocked mid-session with HTTP 401 'bad IP reputation'); the two decree PDFs themselves (1897 and its 817/1435H amendment) could not be fetched directly (SSL failure / empty proxied content); and the Annex's 27 مضافة classification is an inference from comparing Article 3's pre/post-amendment wording plus a matching contemporary news account (almuraba.net, 2014), not a portal-native per-article 'added' marking. Cross-verified in fine-grained numeric detail against almuraba.net (independently confirms the 1435H amendment's 14-day rare-parts turnaround, 2-year minimum warranty, and 27-article annex count). **Disclosed, unresolved 9-Hijri-year date conflict**: this Regulation's own preamble cites the base Law's amending Royal Decree No. 5 as dated 11/06/1398H, while the corpus's own base-law track (verified via two independently-dated BOE archives) records 11/6/1389H for the same decree — neither source is preferred; both are recorded as-is. A mixed Arabic-Indic/Eastern-Arabic numeral inconsistency in the Article-3 amendment note is preserved verbatim as a source artifact, not corrected. Arabic governs; not legal advice.
tracks.source_authority: Ministry of Commerce Resolution No. (1897), dated 24/5/1401H (30 March 1981G), issued pursuant to Article 3 of the Commercial Agencies Law (Royal Decree No. 11, 20/02/1382H — itself amended by Royal Decree No. 5, dated 11/06/1398H per this Regulation's own preamble, though this corpus's own already-verified commercial_agencies base-law track records 11/6/1389H for the same decree, a 9-Hijri-year discrepancy disclosed and left unresolved; and Royal Decree No. 32, 10/08/1400H). Amended by Ministry of Commerce Resolution No. (817), dated 24/8/1435H (Article 3 of the main body; the entire 27-article Annex on maintenance/spare-parts/warranty obligations is attributed to this same 1435H resolution by inference, not an explicit per-article portal marking). laws.boe.gov.sa: no dedicated lawId page for this Regulation (only for the base Law). PRIMARY mc.gov.sa's own live Regulations portal, reached via the r.jina.ai reader-proxy after direct curl/WebFetch and a Wayback Machine snapshot of the same URL both hit BotDetect CAPTCHA bot-detection; SECONDARY nezams.com, qistas.com, thelawsa.com, corporate-lawyer.org (decree number/date) and almuraba.net (a contemporary 2014 news report independently matching multiple specific figures in the 1435H amendment).

tracks.display_name_ar: اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مهنة المحاسبة والمراجعة
tracks.display_name_en: Implementing Regulation of the Law of the Accounting and Auditing Profession
tracks.notes: Implementing Regulation of the Law of the Accounting and Auditing Profession «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مهنة المحاسبة والمراجعة» — Ministry of Commerce Resolution No. (00658), dated 14/11/1442H, issued under Article 22 of the base Law (Royal Decree M/59, 27/7/1442H); a companion instrument to this corpus's already-ingested accounting_auditing_law track (the base Law's own 22 articles are NOT re-ingested here). **15 records: 14 اصلية / 1 معدلة** (Article 6, paragraphs 4-5), flat structure with no أبواب/فصول. **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_2** — PRIMARY is SOCPA's own official PDF, whose direct fetch fails domain-wide (connection reset) and was instead recovered via a single Wayback Machine snapshot. **Critical extraction finding, fully disclosed**: the PDF's own embedded font/ToUnicode mapping systematically transposes Arabic letters on both pdftotext and PyMuPDF extraction (e.g. 'في'→'يف', 'المادة'→'املادة') — resolved by using Tesseract OCR of 300dpi page-image renders as the primary text source (not subject to this defect), cross-checking every digit/percentage against the (digit-accurate) text-layer extraction, and hand-reconciling residual OCR noise via cross-article boilerplate consistency; this is a disclosed reconstruction methodology, not a claim of clean born-digital text. SECONDARY argaam.com (verbatim match on the Article 9 Saudi-staffing percentage table and Article 5's 6%/1000-hour figures) and a 2021 darkhabr.com Wayback snapshot (verbatim match on Article 3/4/5 thresholds); the founding decree citation independently confirmed via a 9 Aug 2022 Wayback snapshot of the Umm al-Qura Gazette's own approval notice (its companion issuance-notice page could not be reached by any method this pass). **2025 amendment confirmed but pre-amendment text NOT recovered**: Ministry of Commerce Resolution No. (28), 3/2/1447H, transferred Article 6's licensing decision authority from the Ministry to SOCPA (the Authority) within fifteen business days, per qanoonsa.com (quoting the resolution number/date/new wording and Umm al-Qura Gazette Issue 5099, 1 Aug 2025G) — this track's only available PDF snapshot already postdates the amendment, so the pre-2025 wording of Article 6(4)-(5) could not be independently diffed; disclosed as an honest gap. Article 9's Saudi-staffing percentage table is linearized into colon-separated sentences without altering any value. Arabic governs; not legal advice.
tracks.source_authority: Ministry of Commerce Resolution No. (00658), dated 14/11/1442H (2 July 2021G), issued under Article 22 of the Law of the Accounting and Auditing Profession (Royal Decree M/59, 27/7/1442H); administered by the Saudi Authority for Auditors and Accountants (SOCPA). Article 6, paragraphs (4) and (5), amended by Ministry of Commerce Resolution No. (28), dated 3/2/1447H (28 July 2025G), pursuant to Council of Ministers Resolution No. (571), 5/8/1446H, transferring licensing-application authority from the Ministry to the Authority. PRIMARY SOCPA's own official PDF, whose direct fetch fails domain-wide (connection reset) and was instead recovered via a single Wayback Machine snapshot (13 Dec 2025) fetched with the archive's raw/id_ modifier; the PDF's own text layer carries a systematic letter-transposition defect, so Tesseract OCR of 300dpi page-image renders was used as the primary text source, with the (digit-accurate) text-layer extraction cross-checked for every numeral/percentage and every clause hand-reconciled; SECONDARY argaam.com and a 2021 darkhabr.com Wayback snapshot (matching figures verbatim); the founding decree's own citation additionally confirmed via a 9 Aug 2022 Wayback snapshot of the Umm al-Qura Gazette's approval notice; the 2025 Article 6 amendment confirmed via qanoonsa.com, which quotes the resolution number/date/new wording and the gazette citation (Issue 5099, 1 Aug 2025G).

tracks.display_name_en: Implementing Regulation of the Commercial Register Law
tracks.notes: Implementing Regulation of the Commercial Register Law «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام السجل التجاري» — Ministry of Commerce Decision No. (288), dated 20 Ramadan 1446H (20 March 2025G), clause 'First' (أولا) thereof, issued under Article 28 of the Commercial Register Law (Royal Decree M/83, 19/3/1446H). **21 records, ALL اصلية** (founding text, no predecessor amendments), flat 21-article structure with no فصول, plus an unnumbered Annex (1) fee schedule referenced by Article 18. **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_2** — laws.boe.gov.sa's only apparently-relevant lawId page was directly verified (via two independently-dated Wayback snapshots) to actually be the BASE Law's own page (29 articles), not a dedicated page for this Regulation; direct fetch of both mc.gov.sa and uqn.gov.sa failed completely (connection-level) this pass. PRIMARY qanoonsa.com (fetched directly, HTTP 200, clean static HTML), cross-checked phrase-by-phrase across nearly every article against Al-Eqtisadiah (aleqt.com, an independent, recognized Saudi financial newspaper) and against the Decision's own preamble/signature text. **Omnibus decision cleanly disambiguated, not a blend**: direct reading of the decision's own text confirms it approves FOUR wholly separate, independently-numbered instruments in one signature — (i) THIS Regulation (clause 'First', 21 articles + Annex 1), (ii) the Trade Names Law's own implementing regulation (sibling track trade_names_regulation, built independently, zero text overlap confirmed by direct comparison), (iii) a transitional subsidiary-register correction mechanism (7 separately-numbered points, a 5-year correction window from 3/4/2025 to 2/4/2030, full text reviewed but NOT ingested here as out of this track's literal title scope), and (iv) controls for trade names registered before the new Law's effective date (out of scope). **Disclosed, uncorrected source anomaly**: Article 19's violation-classification table shows mismatched/reversed parentheses in three of six rows, confirmed present in the source's own raw HTML table structure (not an extraction artifact of this track) and preserved verbatim; the numeral values themselves (500, 1000 riyals) remain unambiguous. Annex (1) preserves a minor source typo (missing definite article 'ال' before 'تجاري'). No أبواب/فصول — flat structure, consistent with this corpus's precedent for comparably short implementing regulations. Arabic governs; not legal advice.
tracks.source_authority: Ministry of Commerce Decision No. (288), dated 20 Ramadan 1446H (20 March 2025G), clause 'First' (أولا) thereof, issued pursuant to Article 28 of the Commercial Register Law (Royal Decree M/83, 19/3/1446H). Published in Umm al-Qura Official Gazette, Issue (5079), 30 March 2025G; effective 3 April 2025G. Decision 288 is a single omnibus instrument whose OTHER three clauses approve three separate instruments — the Trade Names Law's own implementing regulation (a sibling track, trade_names_regulation, built independently and containing no overlapping text), a transitional subsidiary-register correction mechanism (5-year window, 7 separately-numbered points, out of scope for this track), and controls for trade names registered before the new Law's effective date (out of scope) — none of which are within this track's scope. laws.boe.gov.sa's only related lawId page was found, via two independently-dated Wayback snapshots, to actually host the BASE Commercial Register Law itself (29 articles), not this Regulation; no dedicated BOE page exists for this Regulation. Direct fetch of mc.gov.sa and uqn.gov.sa both failed completely (connection-level, HTTP 000) this pass; a Wayback snapshot of mc.gov.sa's news bulletin confirmed the joint effective date only (not full text). PRIMARY qanoonsa.com (fetched directly, HTTP 200), cross-checked phrase-by-phrase across nearly every article against an entirely independent secondary source, Al-Eqtisadiah (aleqt.com), and against the decision's own preamble/signature text.

tracks.display_name_en: Implementing Regulation of the Real Estate Brokerage Law
tracks.notes: Implementing Regulation of the Real Estate Brokerage Law «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام الوساطة العقارية» — General Real Estate Authority (REGA) Board of Directors Resolution No. (132/ق), dated 24/06/1444H, issued under Article 23 of the Real Estate Brokerage Law (Royal Decree M/130, 30/11/1443H). **27 records, ALL اصلية**, 8 chapters (فصول): Licensing (2-6), Term/Renewal/Expiry (7-11), Broker Registry (12-13), Practice Controls (14-15), Brokerage Contracts (16-19), Guarantee/Deposit (20-22), Inspection/Enforcement (23-25), Violations Committee (26-27). **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_1_PRIMARY_MULTI_SOURCE** — laws.boe.gov.sa unreachable (connection reset), consistent with a REGA board-level (not royal-decree-level) instrument. PRIMARY x2 independent official government sources in agreement: REGA's own official PDF (SHA-256 verified; a Word-exported PDF whose text layer suffers a documented lam-alif ligature-reordering defect on automated extraction, so this track's governing text was instead visually transcribed page-by-page at 300dpi rather than machine-extracted) and the Umm al-Qura Gazette's own live portal page (direct HTML text extraction) — programmatically compared article-by-article after normalizing diacritics/spacing, matching verbatim in 26 of 27 articles, with a single immaterial one-word preposition variance in Article 14(10) (REGA's text adopted as governing). **An unconfirmed amendment claim explicitly rejected**: an automated fetch-and-summarize tool surfaced a purported amending 'Administrative Decision No. 5-23-م-23' (1/12/1444H) via lexismiddleeast.com; a direct, non-summarized re-fetch of the identical URL returned HTTP 404, and two other independent sources describing Resolution 132/ق make no mention of any such amendment — this claim is disclosed as likely a fabrication/hallucination of the summarization tool and was NOT applied to any article (all 27 records remain اصلية). Two annex tables (a violations/penalties classification table implementing the base Law's Articles 19-21 penalty framework, and a city/governorate geographic-tier classification table) exist in the source and were content-verified across both primary sources but are NOT ingested as separate structured records this pass — disclosed as a follow-up candidate. A minor 2-3 day gazette-date variance between the directly-observed portal date and two secondary sources is disclosed, not resolved. Arabic governs; not legal advice.
tracks.source_authority: General Real Estate Authority (REGA) Board of Directors Resolution No. (132/ق), dated 24/06/1444H, issued pursuant to Article 23 of the Real Estate Brokerage Law (Royal Decree M/130, 30/11/1443H). Published in the Umm al-Qura Official Gazette (portal-observed date: 25/06/1444H / 18 January 2023G; two secondary sources cite a 2-3 day later gazette-issue date, 27/06/1444H / 20 January 2023G — a minor, immaterial variance disclosed rather than resolved). laws.boe.gov.sa unreachable (connection reset), consistent with this being a REGA board-level regulatory decision rather than a Royal Decree or Council of Ministers resolution. PRIMARY x2 independent official government sources — REGA's own official-site PDF (fetched directly, HTTP 200, SHA-256 verified) and the Umm al-Qura Gazette's own live portal (fetched directly, HTTP 200) — cross-checked programmatically article-by-article, agreeing verbatim in 26 of 27 articles (one immaterial one-word preposition variance in Article 14(10)); decision number/date further corroborated by lexismiddleeast.com (search-indexed) and snadlaw.sa (fetched directly).

tracks.display_name_ar: اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام تملك غير السعوديين للعقار
tracks.display_name_en: Implementing Regulation of the Non-Saudi Real Estate Ownership Law
tracks.notes: Implementing Regulation of the Law on Non-Saudi Real Estate Ownership «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام تملك غير السعوديين للعقار» — a Council of Ministers Resolution, dated 18 Muharram 1448H (3 July 2026G), issued under Article 13 of the base Law (Royal Decree M/14, 19/1/1447H), a document only days old at the time of this verification pass (2026-07-25). **15 records total: 14 articles (ALL اصلية) plus a binding penalty-table annex** (expressly incorporated by the Regulation's own Article 12), flat structure with no فصول/أبواب and no confirmable preamble. **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_1_PRIMARY_MULTI_SOURCE** — two INDEPENDENT Saudi government sources, not aggregators, both fetched live and directly (HTTP 200): the Umm al-Qura Official Gazette's own portal and REGA's own legislation portal (the implementing authority itself), agreeing byte-for-byte, after normalization, in 8 of 14 articles, with the remaining 6 differing only cosmetically — 99.63% overall match. NCAR (the historical laws.boe.gov.sa/Board-of-Experts successor portal), linked from REGA's own page as a third primary reference, could not be reached (TLS reset / HTTP 503); the TIER_1 call rests on the two sources that WERE reached, not three. **Disclosed, NOT resolved**: neither primary source, nor Al-Eqtisadiah's contemporaneous news report, states an explicit Council of Ministers resolution NUMBER or Umm al-Qura gazette ISSUE number; an AI-search synthesis and a single secondary aggregator assert 'Resolution No. 43' / 'gazette Issue 5169', but were NOT adopted here because that same aggregator independently misstates the base Law's own decree date — an honest 'could not confirm' is recorded instead of an unverified number. REGA's page dates the decision itself to ~23 June 2026 while the Gazette dates PUBLICATION to 3 July 2026 — an ordinary ~10-day decision-to-publication gap, disclosed explicitly; the gazette date is adopted as the date of record. This task's own prior-research briefing cited a gazette date of 11 Safar 1448H that could NOT be reproduced this pass; the directly re-observed date (18 Muharram 1448H) is adopted instead. Three penalty-table rows show minor wording variance between the two primary sources (Gazette wording adopted as governing). A source-native inconsistency between Arabic and Latin percent glyphs within the same penalty table is preserved verbatim. Article 9's fee schedule currently lists exactly four geographic zones at a flat 2% fee; this track does not speculate on future additions. Arabic governs; not legal advice.
tracks.source_authority: Council of Ministers Resolution (resolution number NOT confirmed by any primary source — see notes), dated 18 Muharram 1448H (3 July 2026G, the Umm al-Qura Gazette publication date; REGA's own portal separately lists 8 Muharram 1448H / ~23 June 2026G as the decision/issuance date, an ordinary decision-vs-publication gap), issued pursuant to Article 13 of the Law on Non-Saudi Real Estate Ownership (Royal Decree M/14, 19/1/1447H), which required the Council of Ministers to issue this Regulation within 180 days of the base Law's publication. NCAR/laws.boe.gov.sa unreachable (TLS connection reset / HTTP 503) via the link REGA's own page provides to it. PRIMARY x2 independent official government sources in full agreement: the Umm al-Qura Official Gazette's own live portal (fetched directly, HTTP 200) and the General Real Estate Authority's (REGA) own legislation portal (fetched directly, HTTP 200) — 8 of 14 articles byte-identical after normalization, the remaining 6 differing only cosmetically (spacing, comma glyph, one grammatical-gender letter, ZWNJ marks), 99.63% overall match. Al-Eqtisadiah (aleqt.com) independently corroborates the Council of Ministers' approval and dateline but names no resolution number.

tracks.display_name_ar: اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مكافحة الغش التجاري
tracks.notes: Implementing Regulation of the Anti-Commercial Fraud Law «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مكافحة الغش التجاري» — issued to implement the Anti-Commercial Fraud Law (Royal Decree M/19, 23/4/1429H) by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry; the exact ministerial resolution number/date is itself disputed (see source_authority) and recorded transparently rather than silently resolved. **19 records, ALL اصلية** — no formal amendment to this regulation has been located by any source consulted this pass (nezams.com's own metadata states 'لم يجرِ عليه تعديل'), distinct from the base law's own five-times-amended history. Structure: 11 chapter/topical headings (الفصل الأول-الفصل الثامن plus three unlabeled topical sections) spanning Articles 1-19. **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_3** — a single verbatim-reliable secondary source (nezams.com) with zero primary-tier (BOE/mc.gov.sa/ncar.gov.sa/Wayback) access; laws.boe.gov.sa returned HTTP 503/timeout on the base law's own LawDetails page (no distinct page for this Regulation was ever located), mc.gov.sa returned HTTP 503 (r.jina.ai proxy: HTTP 401 'bad IP reputation'), ncar.gov.sa returned HTTP 503/connection-reset, and Wayback Machine's availability-check API confirmed a snapshot exists but content-fetch returned HTTP 403. mrksa.net was fetched and used ONLY for structural corroboration (article count, chapter sequence, Article 19's missing number-label) — NOT for verbatim text — after its HTML showed DeepSeek-AI markdown-rendering fingerprints (133 occurrences, absent from nezams.com) and two concrete substantive divergences: Article 10's trader-notification/foreign-lab detail is summarized away, and Article 17's informant-reward cap reads 50% versus nezams.com's 25% (the figure consistent with the base law's own Article 11). qanoniah.com was JS-rendered and unreadable; almoaqeb.com was unreachable; neither could re-confirm the prior pass's claimed four-source citation agreement. Disclosed discrepancies: the issuing instrument's number/date is genuinely disputed between nezams.com (155, 6/1/1431H) and mrksa.net (55, 20/10/1431H); ncar.gov.sa indexes a third candidate year (1430H). This regulation's Article 1/Article 5 definition of «الجهات المختصة» still matches the base law's ORIGINAL 1429H wording, i.e. it has not been updated to reflect the base law's own later Article 5 amendments — preserved verbatim as likely-stale-but-not-formally-amended. Two purely mechanical nezams.com HTML-transcription artifacts were corrected using mrksa.net's rendering only to confirm word segmentation, not wording. Arabic governs; not legal advice.
tracks.source_authority: Ministerial Resolution disputed between two directly-fetched secondary sources: nezams.com's metadata table cites 'القرار الوزاري رقم 155 وتاريخ 6/1/1431هـ' (published 29/1/1431هـ), while mrksa.net's own preamble instead reads 'قرار وزاري رقم (55) وتاريخ 20/10/1431هـ'; both candidates issued pursuant to the Anti-Commercial Fraud Law (Royal Decree M/19, 23/4/1429H) by the Minister of Commerce and Industry. Applying/administering authority: Ministry of Commerce (General Administration for Combating Commercial Fraud). laws.boe.gov.sa: no distinct lawId page for this Implementing Regulation was located (only the base law's own page surfaced), and that page itself was unreachable this pass (HTTP 503 / 15000ms timeout); mc.gov.sa (HTTP 503 / r.jina.ai HTTP 401), ncar.gov.sa (HTTP 503/connection reset), and Wayback Machine content-fetch (HTTP 403) were all also unreachable. PRIMARY nezams.com (governing verbatim source for all 19 articles); SECONDARY mrksa.net (structural corroboration only — article count and chapter sequence — after two concrete substantive divergences, including a 25%-vs-50% informant-reward-cap discrepancy, revealed AI-regeneration fingerprints in its article-body text); qanoniah.com (JS-rendered, unreadable) and almoaqeb.com (unreachable) could not independently corroborate the prior pass's four-source claim.

tracks.display_name_ar: اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام رسوم التصرفات العقارية
tracks.display_name_en: Implementing Regulation of the Real Estate Transaction Tax Law
tracks.notes: Implementing Regulation of the Real Estate Transaction Tax Law «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام رسوم/ضريبة التصرفات العقارية» — ZATCA Board Decision No. (01-03-25), 24/09/1446H, published Umm al-Qura Issue (5080), 11/10/1446H, entering into force on the same date as the base RETT Law (~9-10 April 2025G). **15 records, ALL اصلية** — no amendment found since issuance through the current date. **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_1** — the full verbatim Arabic text of all 15 articles was extracted directly from the born-digital PDF published on the issuing Authority's own site (zatca.gov.sa, HTTP 200, no proxy needed), reconciled from two independent extraction pipelines (Tesseract Arabic OCR of 300dpi page renders, cross-checked against PyMuPDF character-exact geometric extraction) to correct a systematic Arabic bidi/justification ordering defect and confusable list-marker digit/letter OCR misreads. Corroborated by snadlaw.sa (article-by-article topic match) and qanoonsa.com (Gazette issue confirmation). Important correction disclosed rather than silently accepted: the commissioning brief's claim that this Regulation 'was later amended per SPA (N2095607) and argaam.com' does not hold — those items predate this Regulation's own issuance by eleven months and in fact describe amendments to the PRE-EXISTING predecessor Regulation (Ministerial Resolution No. 712, 15/2/1442H), which this Regulation's own Article 14 names twice (for transitional/grandfathering purposes) without expressly repealing it by name. uqn.gov.sa (Gazette portal, HTTP 503) and the Wayback Machine (network-layer blocked) could not be directly fetched, so the Gazette issue/date rest on secondary-source corroboration rather than a direct primary fetch, while the Regulation's operative TEXT itself was fetched directly and primarily from zatca.gov.sa. A small residual risk of unflagged character-level OCR error in long prose passages is disclosed rather than assumed away. Arabic governs; not legal advice.
tracks.source_authority: Board of Directors of the Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA) Decision No. (01-03-25), dated 24/09/1446H (24 March 2025G), issued under Article 20 of the Real Estate Transaction Tax Law (Royal Decree M/84, 19/3/1446H), published in the Umm al-Qura Gazette, Issue (5080), dated 11/10/1446H (~9 April 2025G). laws.boe.gov.sa: no dedicated lawId page for this Board-level Implementing Regulation (consistent with this corpus's vat_regulation and income_tax_regulation tracks) — only the base RETT Law's own lawId page surfaces. PRIMARY zatca.gov.sa's own official-site PDF (fetched directly, no proxy needed); SECONDARY snadlaw.sa and qanoonsa.com (article-by-article topic/Gazette-issue corroboration); uqn.gov.sa (Gazette portal) and the Wayback Machine returned unreachable this pass (HTTP 503/401; egress-blocked respectively).

tracks.display_name_ar: اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مكافحة المخدرات والمؤثرات العقلية
tracks.display_name_en: Implementing Regulation of the Anti-Narcotics and Psychotropic Substances Control Law
tracks.notes: Implementing Regulation ('Executive List') of the Anti-Narcotics and Psychotropic Substances Control Law «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مكافحة المخدرات والمؤثرات العقلية» — Council of Ministers Resolution No. 201, 10/6/1431H, published 6/7/1431H, effective ~mid-July 2010. The SAME enacting resolution also carries a second, textually separate operative clause amending a DIFFERENT prior resolution (No. 203, 14/7/1425H) on narcotics-destruction-committee reward payments — reproduced in the preamble field for transparency only, and excluded from the 40 ingested articles. **40 records, ALL اصلية** — nezams.com's own page metadata states no amendment to date, and no Royal Decree/Council of Ministers Resolution amending these 40 articles was found via web search. Structure: a flat sequence of 40 مواد with NO باب/فصل division and no topical section headers at all, honestly left absent rather than invented; Articles 2 and 34 embed substance/dosage HTML tables, linearized to plain text preserving every cell. **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_3 (single full-text primary source)** — all 40 مواد rest on ONE full-text source (nezams.com), materially weaker than the base law's own multi-source standard. The official BOE portal (HTTP 503/connection reset), the MOI PDF (connection reset), and Wayback Machine content ('Blocked by egress policy') were all attempted and failed. qistas.com independently matched only the enacting-resolution PREAMBLE word-for-word — not any of the 40 articles; almehleky.sa gave topical, non-verbatim corroboration for only 3 of 40 articles. A fourth source (zarah.com.sa PDF) was fetched but rejected: systematic Arabic ligature/digit-reversal corruption and its content terminates before ever reaching this Regulation's text. Other disclosed items: decorative in-word tatweel characters were cleaned per this corpus's standard normalization rule (no semantic change); a nezams.com site-navigation sentence was stripped from Article 34; an en-dash-vs-tatweel sub-item-marker styling inconsistency between the articles and the preamble was preserved verbatim as a low-stakes formatting uncertainty rather than normalized. Arabic governs; not legal advice.
tracks.source_authority: Council of Ministers Resolution No. 201, dated 10/6/1431H (24 May 2010), issued pursuant to Article 69 of the Anti-Narcotics and Psychotropic Substances Control Law (Royal Decree M/39, 8/7/1426H), which directed the Ministries of Interior, Justice and Health to prepare this Implementing Regulation; published in the Official Gazette 6/7/1431H (18 June 2010), effective 30 days thereafter per the Regulation's own Article 40. laws.boe.gov.sa (lawId be479758-9a84-4e94-b1d3-a9a700f19454), the MOI-hosted PDF, and Wayback Machine content-fetch were all confirmed unreachable this pass (HTTP 503/connection-reset; 'Blocked by egress policy'). PRIMARY nezams.com's dedicated regulation page (fetched directly via curl with a browser User-Agent; HTTP 406 without one, HTTP 200 with); SECONDARY qistas.com (word-for-word match of the enacting-resolution preamble only, not any of the 40 substantive مواد) and almehleky.sa (topical, non-verbatim corroboration of 3 of 40 articles); a fourth source (zarah.com.sa PDF) was fetched but rejected for systematic Arabic ligature/digit-reversal corruption and for not actually containing the Regulation's text.

tracks.display_name_en: Implementing Regulation of the Anti-Concealment Law
tracks.notes: Implementing Regulation of the Anti-Concealment Law «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مكافحة التستر» — issued pursuant to Article 19 of the Anti-Concealment Law (Royal Decree M/4, 1/1/1442H); a follow-up track to this corpus's existing anti_concealment (base law) track. **18 records, ALL اصلية** — no amendment to this Regulation has been located this pass; this reflects 'no amendment found', not 'confirmed no amendment exists'. Structure: 9 unnumbered topical section headings (no الفصل/الباب labels, unlike the base law) spanning Articles 1-18, matching the source PDF's own table of contents. **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_2** — the full text (18 articles, 9 pages) was read visually in full from mc.gov.sa's own official PDF (pdftotext produced systematic Arabic character-substitution corruption, so direct visual reading of 200dpi page renders was used instead), corroborated by an independent second official source (a Saudi Press Agency article matching the PDF's content, structure and timing exactly) — but NOT raised to TIER_1 because no second independent full-text copy exists for article-by-article literal comparison, and because the founding ministerial resolution's own signed text (No. 00479, 20/7/1442H) was never directly read — its number/date rest on convergent indirect evidence only, explicitly disclosed as such. uqn.gov.sa, the Wayback Machine, r.jina.ai, laws.boe.gov.sa, and qanoniah.com were all attempted and failed — mirroring the identical three-way failure pattern already documented in the base law's own track. mc.gov.sa itself required resolving an incomplete server-side TLS certificate chain (missing intermediate) — a routine client-side fix, not a bypass of any access control. Arabic governs; not legal advice.
tracks.source_authority: Ministerial Decision No. (00479), dated 20/7/1442H — confirmed only via convergent indirect evidence (an indexed Umm al-Qura gazette page title, aggregated web-search citations, and the source PDF's own embedded creation-date metadata, coinciding exactly), NOT via direct reading of the signed resolution text itself. Issued pursuant to Article 19 of the Anti-Concealment Law (Royal Decree M/4, 1/1/1442H), which requires the Minister of Commerce, in agreement with the Minister of Interior, to issue this Regulation within 180 days of the Law's publication. Administering authority: Ministry of Commerce, coordinating with the Ministries of Municipal & Rural Affairs/Housing, Human Resources & Social Development, Environment/Water/Agriculture, and the General Authority of Zakat and Tax. PRIMARY mc.gov.sa's own PDF (fetched directly after resolving an incomplete server-side TLS chain); SECONDARY a Saudi Press Agency (SPA) news article and the Ministry's own news page independently corroborating content, timing and coordinating ministries. laws.boe.gov.sa (HTTP 503), uqn.gov.sa (returns only the site's cover page), Wayback Machine content-fetch ('Blocked by egress policy') and r.jina.ai (HTTP 401) were all unreachable this pass.

tracks.display_name_en: Implementing Regulation of the Privatization Law
tracks.notes: Implementing Regulation of the Privatization Law «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام التخصيص» — originally issued by National Center for Privatization Board Decision No. (ق-9/2021), 23/4/1443H (159 articles, 8 أبواب), amended by Board Decision No. (1/4/2023), 18/6/1445H, published Umm al-Qura Gazette 21/7/1445H, currently in force as a 169-article consolidated text (8 أبواب unchanged). **169 records: 140 اصلية / 19 معدلة / 10 مضافة (0 ملغاة)** — the 10 wholly new articles and 19 substantively-amended articles were each confirmed by direct content comparison against the original 159-article text, not inferred from the count difference alone. **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_1** for the governing text itself — the current 169-article text was fetched live and directly from the Umm al-Qura Gazette portal (HTTP 200, no proxy or secondary aggregator), with the article count and 8-باب structure verified programmatically and independently corroborated by a third news source (ajel.sa, explicitly citing '169 مادة'). A caveat applies to the per-article اصلية/معدلة/مضافة classification: the original 2021 PDF used for comparison suffers systematic pdftotext letter-order corruption, so it could not be used as governing text — only for structural counts and a targeted (not exhaustive) comparison; a representative sample surfaced amendments not confined to the count-changed أبواب. The 140 articles classified اصلية reflect 'no change detected in the comparisons performed', not an exhaustive literal audit of all 140 — disclosed honestly as a residual gap. Other disclosed items: laws.boe.gov.sa (connection reset), Wayback Machine (policy block) and r.jina.ai (HTTP 401) were all unreachable; the original decision's precise Gregorian/Gazette-publication dates were only approximated via a 2022 news citation; a journalistic attribution of the original decision to 'مجلس الوزراء' conflicts with the decision's own title attributing it to the NCP Board — the official decision title was preferred, with the conflicting press wording disclosed. This track is explicitly disambiguated from two companion NCP instruments, neither built here. Arabic governs; not legal advice.
tracks.source_authority: National Center for Privatization (NCP) Board Decision No. (1/4/2023), dated 18/6/1445H (31 December 2023G), amending the original NCP Board Decision No. (ق-9/2021), dated 23/4/1443H, both issued under Article 44 of the Privatization Law (Royal Decree M/63, 5/8/1442H). Amended text published in the Umm al-Qura Official Gazette, dated 21/7/1445H (2 February 2024G). laws.boe.gov.sa: unreachable this pass (connection reset), and no dedicated lawId page is known to exist for NCP Board decisions. PRIMARY uqn.gov.sa (Umm al-Qura Gazette portal), fetched directly and live (HTTP 200) — the actual governing text of all 169 currently-effective articles; SECONDARY a 2021 argaamplus.s3.amazonaws.com PDF of the original 159-article decision (used only to confirm original article/chapter counts and identify amendment locations, owing to systematic letter-order corruption in its pdftotext extraction), further corroborated by argaam.com, ajel.sa, alarabiya.net, snadlaw.sa, qanoonsa.com and aunklaw.com. Wayback Machine and r.jina.ai were both unreachable/blocked this pass.

tracks.display_name_en: Implementing Regulation of the Chambers of Commerce Law
tracks.notes: Implementing Regulation of the Chambers of Commerce Law «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام الغرف التجارية» — Ministerial Decision No. (10), 11/1/1443H, published Umm al-Qura Gazette 20 August 2021; amended once, by Ministerial Decision No. 87, 12/5/1447H (3 November 2025), which lowered Article 10's chamber-board-size tiers from four bands to three. **63 records: 62 اصلية / 1 معدلة (Article 10) / 0 مضافة / 0 ملغاة.** Structure: an unnumbered أحكام تمهيدية section, two أبواب (الغرفة; اتحاد الغرف) each split into numbered فصول, and a closing أحكام ختامية section, spanning Articles 1-63. A pending draft amendment to Article 44 (public consultation Jan 2025, restructuring the performance-evaluation advisory-body requirement) was explicitly checked and found NOT adopted as of this pass — Article 44 is recorded here in its original, still-current form, with the draft text disclosed separately rather than silently substituted. **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_2** — the live Umm al-Qura site redirects to a JavaScript-rendered Vue SPA with no article text in raw HTML, so a 2022-08-18 Wayback Machine snapshot (an older WordPress-era version of the same page, raw HTML) was used as the primary source, cross-checked paragraph-by-paragraph and table-by-table against an independent semi-official PDF from the Federation of Saudi Chambers with zero content divergence except one formatting-only difference in Article 15. The Article 10 amendment was sourced from qanoonsa.com (a non-governmental legislative-tracking site) rather than a raw/scanned copy of the Gazette itself (a direct link returned 404), independently corroborated by akhbaar24.com. Not raised to TIER_1 because no dedicated laws.boe.gov.sa lawId page exists, the founding Decision No. 10's own signed/sealed text was never directly read, and no raw/scanned Gazette copy was obtained for the Article 10 amendment. Other disclosed items: Article 40's fee table was linearized from a three-column table to numbered prose with every figure cross-verified identical between sources; the source Gazette archive is internally inconsistent in sub-item punctuation between structurally-parallel Articles 34 and 53, preserved as published rather than harmonized. Arabic governs; not legal advice.
tracks.source_authority: Ministerial Decision No. (10), dated 11/1/1443H — confirmed only indirectly, via an explicit recital in a later amendment decision (Ministerial Decision No. 87, 12/5/1447H), not via direct access to Decision No. 10's own signed text — issued under Article 64 of the Chambers of Commerce Law (Royal Decree M/37, 22/4/1442H), published in the Umm al-Qura Gazette 20 August 2021. Latest confirmed amendment: Ministerial Decision No. 87, dated 12/5/1447H (3 November 2025), amending Article 10 only. laws.boe.gov.sa: no dedicated lawId page for this Implementing Regulation (only the base law's own page exists). PRIMARY the Umm al-Qura Gazette, via a 2022-08-18 Wayback Machine snapshot (the live uqn.gov.sa site is a JavaScript-rendered SPA with no raw-HTML article content); SECONDARY the Federation of Saudi Chambers' own official PDF (fsc.org.sa) — paragraph-by-paragraph and table-by-table cross-check with zero content differences aside from one formatting-only sub-clause-numbering divergence; the Article 10 amendment corroborated via qanoonsa.com and akhbaar24.com.

tracks.display_name_en: Implementing Regulation of the State Revenue Law
tracks.notes: Implementing Regulation of the State Revenue Law «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام إيرادات الدولة» — Ministerial Resolution No. (860), dated 13/3/1432H, issued by the Minister of Finance, amended by Ministerial Resolution No. (901), dated 24/2/1439H. **65 records: 60 اصلية / 4 معدلة / 1 مضافة**, organized into 6 numbered فصول, confirmed directly from the source PDF's own printed chapter-title pages. **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_2** — the Ministry of Finance's own official PDF was fetched directly and every page was rendered as an image and read visually (eliminating an automated OCR artifact this corpus's own tooling documented as reversing word order on this file family), but only Articles 1-8 could be cross-verified word-for-word against a second independent source (qanoniah.com's backend API, before its paywall gate was reached) — Articles 9-65 rest on the single MOF PDF, visually verified but without a second source's full text. Disclosed discrepancies: ncar.gov.sa hosts this document but every direct-fetch attempt (live and via Wayback) failed at the TCP/TLS layer or returned a content-free SPA shell; adf.gov.sa and the direct Umm al-Qura gazette article URL were likewise unreachable, leaving that gazette corroboration resting on a search-engine snippet only; the pre-901 (original 1432H) wording of the five touched articles could not be recovered (the only located 1432H copy is a scanned image PDF with an unusable OCR layer), so original_1432h_text is honestly null for every article rather than fabricated; qanoniah.com's own metadata carries a conflicting issuance-date tag for Resolution 901 versus the MOF PDF's own printed date — '24/2/1439H' (Safar) is treated as correct and the discrepancy is disclosed rather than silently resolved; Article 64 is a generic, non-specific repeal clause naming no predecessor regulation, so repealed_predecessor.confirmed is false — an honest could-not-confirm; the five-article amendment scope rests on matching the current text against a 2017 draft-stage mof.gov.sa announcement rather than a direct diff against the final adopted text or the (unusable) original PDF, so it should be read as 'five articles independently confirmed changed', not an exhaustive guarantee against other undetected wording shifts. Arabic governs; not legal advice.
tracks.source_authority: Ministerial Resolution No. (860), dated 13/3/1432H, issued by the Minister of Finance pursuant to Article 29 of the State Revenue Law (Royal Decree M/68, 18/11/1431H); amended by Ministerial Resolution No. (901), dated 24/2/1439H, signed by Minister of Finance Mohammed bin Abdullah Al-Jadaan. Effective from 20/3/1432H (independently corroborated by a Saudi Press Agency news item dated 22 Rabi al-Thani 1432H / 27 March 2011, which also confirms the original 64-article count and the Article-29 authority citation). laws.boe.gov.sa: the base law's own LawDetails page (reached via Wayback) contains no link, section, or reference to this Implementing Regulation at all, consistent with this corpus's documented pattern that BOE does not catalogue Ministerial-Resolution-level executive regulations as their own lawId records. PRIMARY the Ministry of Finance's own document-library PDF (mof.gov.sa), fetched directly (HTTP 200) and transcribed by direct visual reading of every rendered page image (bypassing a documented reversed-word-order text-extraction artifact); SECONDARY qanoniah.com's backend API, which independently corroborates Articles 1-8 word-for-word plus the founding/amending decree numbers, gazette citation (Umm al-Qura issue 4705), and in-force status. ncar.gov.sa and adf.gov.sa/uqn.gov.sa were unreachable this pass (connection resets, soft-404s, or content-free SPA shells).

tracks.display_name_en: Implementing Regulation of the Weapons and Ammunition Law
tracks.notes: Implementing Regulation of the Weapons and Ammunition Law «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام الأسلحة والذخائر» — Ministerial Resolution No. (23), dated 19/1/1428H, issued by the Minister of Interior, published in Umm al-Qura gazette issue (4159), 13/7/1428H. **19 records: 7 اصلية / 12 معدلة** — this Regulation carries NO independent article numbering of its own; every record is keyed to, and cross-referenced against, the base law's own article numbers (only 19 of the base law's 63 articles carry attached implementing text in this source). **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_3** — the primary source (qadha.org.sa's consolidated PDF) has a digital text layer corrupted by a systemic font-encoding defect requiring Tesseract OCR reconstruction, and full cross-verification is available for only 2 of the 19 articles (qanoonsa.com, Articles 3 and 5). Disclosed discrepancies: the source itself gives conflicting founding-decree numbers — '23' (preamble/index) vs '33' (amendment-history table) — with '23' adopted as correct; Ministerial Resolution 549 (4/2/1446H) adds a new paragraph to Article 23's regulation that the source states explicitly 'لم تسر بعد' (has not yet taken effect), recorded with pending status disclosed; a FIFTH amendment (Minister of Interior Resolution 1938, 10/4/1446H), independently discovered via uqn.gov.sa, adds a medical/toxicology screening requirement to Article 9's regulation and postdates the qadha.org.sa consolidated source, resting on a single direct gazette source without a second independent confirmation; pre-amendment original wording is not preserved for most amended articles; Article 13/3(b)'s text could not be confirmed with confidence due to page-layout ambiguity and is flagged rather than fabricated; Article 3's own implementing regulation was relocated in full into Article 9's regulation by Resolution 5656; fee-schedule annexes referenced by Articles 12 and 25 are out of scope. Arabic governs; not legal advice.
tracks.source_authority: Ministerial Resolution No. (23), dated 19/1/1428H, issued by the Minister of Interior (Prince Naif bin Abdulaziz) pursuant to Article 63 of the Weapons and Ammunition Law (Royal Decree M/45, 25/7/1426H); published in the official Umm al-Qura gazette, issue (4159), dated 13/7/1428H. Amended four times as previously known (Ministerial Resolutions 3499, 14/4/1434H; 274833, 1/11/1437H; 5656, 6/5/1442H; 549, 4/2/1446H) plus a FIFTH amendment independently discovered this pass (Minister of Interior Resolution No. 1938, dated 10/4/1446H, published 29/4/1446H), confirmed directly via the official Umm al-Qura gazette site (uqn.gov.sa). laws.boe.gov.sa: no dedicated lawId page located for this Regulation — the only related hit was a scanned-image reproduction of the base law's own royal decree. PRIMARY qadha.org.sa (the Saudi Judicial Scientific Society)'s own consolidated PDF, whose digital text layer is corrupted by a systemic ToUnicode/font-encoding defect and was therefore reconstructed via Tesseract OCR on rendered page images; SECONDARY qanoonsa.com, corroborating only 2 of the 19 articles carrying Regulation text (Articles 3 and 5) verbatim; uqn.gov.sa, fetched directly to confirm the fifth, previously-unknown amendment. The source carries an unresolved internal conflict over its own founding decree number (23 in two places vs. 33 in the amendment-history table).

tracks.display_name_ar: اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مزاولة المهن الهندسية
tracks.display_name_en: Implementing Regulation of the Law of Practicing Engineering Professions
tracks.notes: Implementing Regulation of the Law of Practicing Engineering Professions «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مزاولة المهن الهندسية» — Ministerial Decision No. (4/4400942200), dated 26/5/1445H, published Umm al-Qura gazette issue (5013), 16/6/1445H. **18 records, ALL اصلية**, flat structure of 18 sequentially numbered مواد with no أبواب/فصول grouping and no inline per-article titles. **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_2** — a single official government primary source (uqn.gov.sa, live HTML text) was reached and cross-checked article-by-article against an independent secondary source (qanoonsa.com) with a full 18/18 verbatim match; TIER_1 was not reached because both laws.boe.gov.sa and saudieng.sa were unreachable live this pass, and the Wayback Machine's CDX metadata API confirmed the saudieng.sa file's existence and stability but its content-serving path returned 'Blocked by egress policy'. Disclosed discrepancies: this Regulation explicitly supersedes a 2018 original (Ministerial Resolution 38315) via a general, not-specifically-named repeal clause — that original's full text could not be independently confirmed this pass and is honestly NOT reconstructed or guessed at; two source-level structural anomalies are preserved verbatim rather than silently corrected — Article 4 skips the alphabetic label 'ج-' for its third accreditation category, and Article 7's numbering jumps from item '2-' directly to item '4-' with no '3-' at all, both confirmed present character-for-character in both sources; the gazette issue number (5013) appears only in the qanoonsa.com secondary source, not in uqn.gov.sa's own Article 18 text, though the Gregorian publication date is independently confirmed via both uqn.gov.sa pages' own metadata. This track is entirely separate from, and does not modify, this corpus's existing engineering_practice (base law) track. Arabic governs; not legal advice.
tracks.source_authority: Decision No. (4/4400942200) of the Minister of Municipal, Rural, and Housing Affairs, dated 26/5/1445H, issued under Article 16 of the Law of Practicing Engineering Professions (Royal Decree M/36, 19/4/1438H) and Supreme Royal Order No. (17103), dated 26/3/1442H (transferring supervision of the Saudi Council of Engineers from the Ministry of Commerce to this Ministry). the 16 amended articles rest on a SINGLE source (HRSD's current PDF) alone, manually corrected for a confirmed, disclosed text-layer character-order defect that made automated extraction unsafe — no independent second source was reachable for these 16 articles this pass. **NO SINGLE PROMULGATING DECISION NUMBER**: unlike the older 1397H predecessor regulation (Civil Service Council Resolution No. 1), this regulation's own text carries no single self-contained issuing decision number — its basis is Article 39 of the Civil Service Law plus the reform committee formed by Council of Ministers Resolution No. (75), 29/1/1440H, without one dedicated final-approval decision number/date located this pass. **CURRENCY DETERMINATION**: this track independently investigated whether the older 1397H regulation remains governing, or whether this 1440H regulation has effectively superseded it — concluded the 1440H regulation IS the currently governing text (the 1397H document is itself only a historical index pointing to ten scattered, dormant sub-regulations that this 1440H regulation consolidates and replaces in substance; a dedicated reform committee explicitly produced this 1440H text; it remains actively amended through 1444H while the 1397H document has been frozen since 1438H) — but NO single explicit repeal clause naming the 1397H instrument was found, so this conclusion rests on convergent circumstantial/structural evidence, not a direct repeal citation, disclosed as such. Other disclosed items: a cover-page-vs-portal publication date discrepancy (1440H cover vs. 1441H HRSD portal metadata); footnote-to-article misattribution errors caught and corrected during manual review; Article 39 carries an amendment decree but shows no textual change from 1440H (possibly non-substantive); Article 105's single cited amendment does not fully account for additional wording differences observed; a genuine source typo on the Chapter 11 divider page; stale «وزارة الخدمة المدنية» institutional naming persists in several unamended articles pending piecemeal updates. Arabic governs; not legal advice.

tracks.notes: Implementing Regulation of the Electronic Transactions Law «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام التعاملات الإلكترونية» — DGA Board Decision No. (م-8-6), 3 Ramadan 1445H, 8 فصول. **25 records, ALL اصلية** (no subsequent article-level amendment found since issuance). **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_2_PRIMARY_SECONDARY_CROSS_VERIFIED** — a single reachable official primary source (Umm al-Qura Gazette), with no independent SECOND government source reachable this pass (dga.gov.sa Cloudflare-blocked; laws.boe.gov.sa unreachable), but cross-verified verbatim against an independent press outlet (argaam.com) for two full articles, plus multiple secondary legal-database corroborations of the decision number/date. tracks.display_name_ar: اللائحتان التنفيذيتان لنظام الكهرباء (مهمات الهيئة ومهمات الوزارة)
tracks.display_name_en: Electricity Law Implementing Regulations -- the Authority's part and the Ministry's part (Royal Decree M/44, 16/5/1442H, Article 22)
tracks.notes: Electricity Law Implementing Regulations «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام الكهرباء» — issued as TWO SEPARATE INSTRUMENTS under Article 22 of the Electricity Law (M/44, 16/5/1442H), which splits the implementing-regulation mandate in two: paragraph (1) tasks the Minister of Energy with the Ministry's-duties regulation, paragraph (2) tasks the Authority's Board with the Authority's-duties regulation. This track COMBINES both instruments into one track (electricity_regulation) with a clear internal split (an instrument_part field of 'authority' or 'ministry' plus the original per-instrument article numbering preserved on every record) rather than splitting them into two tracks, because both instruments issue from the same enabling article, were adopted roughly a week apart, were published in consecutive Umm al-Qura Gazette issues (4911/4912) a week apart, and govern the same overarching Law — while preserving that they are legally two independent instruments (different issuing authorities, decision numbers/dates, independent article numbering starting at Article 1 in each, different Gazette issue numbers). **Authority's part**: Board Decision No. (43/02), 13/4/1443H, 56 articles/10 chapters. **Ministry's part**: Minister's Decision No. (1443/1728/01), 8/3/1443H, 36 articles/14 chapters. Combined: **92 records, ALL اصلية** (56 + 36 = 92). **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_3** for both instruments — sera.gov.sa, laws.boe.gov.sa, and uqn.gov.sa's live portal were all unreachable this pass and web.archive.org is egress-blocked, so the full verbatim text of both instruments rests on a single non-government aggregator (qanoonsa.com) rather than a directly-fetched or Wayback-mediated government source; a follow-up re-verification against laws.boe.gov.sa or sera.gov.sa is explicitly recommended once reachable. Disclosed items: the Ministry's decision was actually signed five weeks before the Authority's decision but published in the Gazette in the reverse order — a documented administrative sequencing quirk; the Authority-part source switches article-numbering digit style from Arabic-Indic to Western partway through, preserved verbatim; an unconfirmed WebSearch-only claim of two further 2023G amending Board decisions could not be confirmed and is NOT adopted; the regulator's pre-rename name is preserved verbatim in the article text itself, with the SERA rename noted for reference only. Arabic governs; not legal advice.
tracks.source_authority: TWO SEPARATE INSTRUMENTS, issued under Article 22 of the Electricity Law (Royal Decree M/44, 16/5/1442H), combined into one track: (1) Water & Electricity Regulatory Authority Board Decision No. (43/02), dated 13/4/1443H (19 November 2021G), 56 articles/10 chapters, published Umm al-Qura Gazette Issue No. (4911), 3 December 2021G; (2) Ministry of Energy Minister's Decision No. (1443/1728/01), dated 8/3/1443H (15 October 2021G), 36 articles/14 chapters, published Umm al-Qura Gazette Issue No. (4912), 10 December 2021G. The regulator was subsequently renamed to the Saudi Electricity Regulatory Authority (SERA) by Council of Ministers Resolution No. (918), dated 28 Shawwal 1445H (7 May 2024G) — confirmed via a direct primary fetch of that Resolution's own text. sera.gov.sa, laws.boe.gov.sa, and uqn.gov.sa's live portal were all unreachable this pass; web.archive.org blocked at this session's egress-policy level. PRIMARY full verbatim text of both instruments, plus the full text of both approval decisions themselves, retrieved directly from qanoonsa.com, with article/chapter counts self-confirmed programmatically against each page's own heading structure.

tracks.notes: Regulation on Ship Registration and Maritime Unit Registration «لائحة تسجيل السفن وقيد الوحدات البحرية», issued by the Transport General Authority (TGA), year of issuance 1441H (specific decision number/date not independently confirmed this pass). tracks.source_authority: Transport General Authority (TGA) Board Decision — decision number and exact Hijri date NOT independently confirmed this pass (TGA's own regulation page displays no decision-number/date field in either historical snapshot examined; two mutually inconsistent AI-summarized candidate decision numbers/dates surfaced by general web search could not be verified against any primary document read directly and are therefore NOT recorded as confirmed). tracks.display_name_en: Implementing Regulation of the Agriculture Law
tracks.notes: Implementing Regulation of the Agriculture Law «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام الزراعة» — Ministerial Decision No. (14967/1/1444), 15/1/1444H, تسعة أبواب. **271 records: 266 اصلية / 5 معدلة** — of the 5 معدلة: Article 1 is amended AND its new text is confirmed and incorporated (2024 addition of a 'serious violation' definition); Articles 45, 98, 208, and 248 are amended-in-law but their new wording is NOT confirmed from any source reachable this pass (a 2026-effective Ministerial Decision approved changes to these four but its attachment text was never published anywhere this pass could reach — MEWA's own current site PDF was positively confirmed to still show the unamended 2022 wording for Article 45) — these four therefore retain their original 2022 text with an explicit status='AMENDED_TEXT_UNCONFIRMED'/text_complete=false flag rather than a fabricated replacement. **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_4_SINGLE_SOURCE_OR_MIXED_CONFIDENCE** — under this corpus's weakest-link policy, 267 of 271 articles would otherwise sit at roughly TIER_2 (a single official primary source, the Umm al-Qura Gazette, with structural/content cross-checks against MEWA's own PDF and qanoonsa.com), but the 4 amended-text-unconfirmed articles pull the whole track's disclosed tier down rather than being averaged away. laws.boe.gov.sa returned HTTP 503 for the base law and appears not to separately index this regulation at all. Other disclosed items: no text of the founding decision's own preamble/signature block was located, so it is unconfirmed whether this decision explicitly repeals prior sectoral regulations that predate the unified 2021 Agriculture Law; a separate public-consultation draft amendment to Article 245 was found referenced but its consultation page was unreachable this pass, so it is NOT incorporated, pending confirmation of whether it was ever adopted; a Farsi yeh character in Article 1 normalized to Arabic yeh; mixed Arabic-Indic/Western digit rendering in the beekeeping chapter preserved verbatim. Arabic governs; not legal advice.

PRIMARY the Umm al-Qura Official Gazette itself (uqn.gov.sa), fetched directly (HTTP 200), clean digital text; CROSS-CHECKED structurally and for content sampling against MEWA's own official-site PDF (a known font-justification character-corruption defect limits it to structural/content use only) and qanoonsa.com (verbatim text of both amending decisions).

tracks.display_name_en: Civil Defense Law -- Subordinate Implementing Regulations (two instruments with fully confirmed text this pass)
tracks.notes: This track covers BOTH subordinate regulations of the Civil Defense Law that could be independently confirmed with full verbatim text this pass — deliberately NOT a single instrument: (1) «لائحة حقوق وواجبات من يستعان بهم في أعمال الدفاع المدني وعلاقتهم بجهاتهم» (Rights and Duties of Persons Recalled for Civil Defense Work), 12 articles, flat, no chapters; (2) «لائحة تنظيم أعمال الإطفاء والإنقاذ بالمديرية العامة للدفاع المدني» (Firefighting and Rescue Regulation), 9 articles plus an unnumbered introductory مقدمة, flat, no chapters. **21 records, ALL اصلية** (12 + 9, 0 معدلة/ملغاة/مضافة). **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_2** for both components (archived official-portal/gazette captures via Wayback, not live fetches). A third candidate instrument, «لائحة النظر في مخالفات نظام ولوائح الدفاع المدني» (Ministerial Decision 12/1/و/5/دف, 18/4/1428H), is confirmed to EXIST via multiple independent secondary sources and is directly cross-referenced by Article 7 of firefighting_rescue, but its only located copy is a 20-page scanned, image-only 2012 PDF with no reliable OCR — its text is deliberately NOT included. A further ~30 sector-specific safety-conditions PDFs (agriculture, laboratories, high-rise buildings, firefighting teams, etc.) are disclosed as an out-of-scope broader universe of Civil Defense implementing instruments, not ingested. A 2020 news report claiming rights_duties has 11 articles conflicts with BOE's own confirmed 12-article text (five independent archival snapshots); the BOE primary count is adopted. firefighting_rescue's precise Gregorian decree date and actual gazette publication date could NOT be confirmed from a live primary source this pass, so no derived 90-day effective date is asserted. A governance-body succession from «مجلس الدفاع المدني» (named in the 1406H base law) to «لجنة الدفاع المدني المكلفة»/«مجلس المخاطر الوطنية» is flagged as a plausible but UNCONFIRMED inference, recorded as a research note only, not adopted as fact. Arabic governs; not legal advice.
tracks.source_authority: TWO subordinate implementing regulations of the Civil Defense Law «نظام الدفاع المدني» (Royal Decree M/10, 10/5/1406H), stored as one track with two internally labeled components. tracks.display_name_en: Implementing Regulation of the Premium (Privileged) Residency Law
tracks.notes: «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام الإقامة المميزة» — Implementing Regulation of the Premium (Privileged) Residency Law. **13 records: 1 اصلية / 12 معدلة** (Article 7 is the only article confirmed byte-identical to the 1440H original by direct comparison). **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_4_SINGLE_SOURCE_OR_MIXED_CONFIDENCE** (graded by the weakest article, not the strongest) — Articles 1-5 carry genuine dual-source verbatim cross-verification (qanoniah.com x aunklaw.com); Articles 6-13 (62% of the document) rest on aunklaw.com alone, with no official/government source reached for any article this pass. preamble_ar is deliberately left empty — no signed/sealed decree preamble text was located on either secondary source. tracks.source_authority: Premium Residency Center Decision No. (4-1440), dated 20/9/1440H (original issuance, per Article 13 of the Premium Residency Law, Royal Decree M/106, 10/9/1440H), comprehensively amended by the Center's Board of Directors Decision No. (7-5-1444), dated 29/12/1444H. tracks.display_name_en: Implementing Regulation of the Water Law for the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture's (MEWA) mandate

Two honest limitations are disclosed: the Ministerial Decision's own number and exact day/month could NOT be confirmed — MEWA's own official cover page leaves both fields blank, and a candidate number/date surfaced in prior research was determined this pass to belong to the SIBLING (76/2) regulation instead, not this one; only the confirmed legal basis (Article 76(1), M/159) is recorded. tracks.display_name_en: Implementing Regulation of the Press and Publications Law
tracks.notes: «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام المطبوعات والنشر» — Implementing Regulation of the Press and Publications Law. **99 records, ALL اصلية** (this is the current post-1439H-amendment consolidated edition; which article(s) the amendment affected could not be attributed from the source alone, an honest gap disclosed rather than an invented per-article history). **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_2** — a single primary source (the Ministry's own PDF, via a November 2024 Wayback snapshot), read in full by direct vision (98 pages) because automated extraction produced word-internal character scrambling. A genuinely independent second full-text source was searched for but not found (WIPO Lex hosts only the base law; qanoniah.com's copy is session-gated; islamport.com was checked directly and found to host only the base law, contradicting an earlier tool-summary that falsely claimed otherwise — recorded as an explicit caution against trusting AI-summarized fetches). One genuine independent corroboration was found: an Umm al-Qura Gazette article confirming Article 69(ج)'s exact subject matter. Disclosed source-level defects preserved verbatim rather than silently fixed: irregular فصل sub-numbering in Baab 2 (a duplicated «الفصل السادس» label, missing فصول 3-5 and 14, and «الفصل السابع عشر» appearing before «السادس عشر») — not renumbered or corrected here; Articles 7 and 16 each substitute a placeholder for a specific procedural clause, kept verbatim; and Article 72 names «الهيئة العامة للمساحة» while Article 73(د), covering the same subject, names «الهيئة العامة للسياحة» — an internal inconsistency in the Ministry's own source, both readings re-verified and neither harmonised. Arabic governs; not legal advice.
tracks.source_authority: Ministerial Decision (Minister of Media) No. (م/و/2759/1/م), dated 16/6/1422H, issued under Article 46 of the Press and Publications Law (Royal Decree M/32, 3/9/1421H); amended by Ministerial Decision No. (91513), dated 9/11/1439H (~23 Jul 2018G) — which specific article(s) that amendment touched could not be determined this pass, as the source is a single flat consolidated document with no in-text changelog and no earlier dated edition to diff against. media.gov.sa returned connection-reset/timeout on every direct-fetch attempt; PRIMARY text instead retrieved via a 23 November 2024 Wayback Machine snapshot of the Ministry's own official PDF. laws.boe.gov.sa has no dedicated lawId page for this ministerial-level regulation.

Two articles from the 1439H founding text were fully REPEALED by the issuing authority's own later decisions with no dedicated slot preserved in the current government-renumbered 1-30 sequence — both articles' full repealed text is preserved verbatim in this track's discrepancy log rather than silently dropped. A LIKELY fifth amendment (replacing «اللجنة الوطنية»/«وزير التجارة» with «المركز السعودي لكود البناء»/«وزير البلديات والإسكان» in Articles 24-25) is indicated by 2026 secondary news coverage and an aggregator-cited decision number, but could NOT be confirmed from any primary gazette source this pass (uqn.gov.sa's server-rendered JS routes and the Wayback Machine's content-serving path were both blocked in this environment) — it is NOT incorporated into the stored text of Articles 24/25, which retain the last independently-confirmed government-primary wording. The exact Umm al-Qura Gazette issue numbers for the founding decree and its three confirmed amendments could not be pinpointed for the same access reason. Arabic governs; not legal advice.
tracks.source_authority: Ministerial Decision No. (1213/ق/أع/39), dated 14/10/1439H, issued by the Minister of Commerce and Investment as Chairman of the Board of the Saudi Standards, Metrology and Quality Organization, under Article 15 of the parent Law on Application of the Saudi Building Code (Royal Decree M/43, 26/4/1438H). tracks.notes: «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام الاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات» — Implementing Regulation of the Telecommunications and Information Technology Law. **108 records, ALL اصلية**. **VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_2_DUAL_OFFICIAL_PRIMARY_BORN_DIGITAL_CROSS_VERIFIED** — two independent official government PDF sources (CST and MCIT), both born-digital, agreeing verbatim after correcting well-documented systematic extraction artifacts, none altering wording or substance: a lam-alif ligature reversal defect, a single reversed cross-reference (corrected from '(41)' to the true 'Article (14)' by comparing both sources against all bracketed references), reversed numbered-paragraph markers, and five articles whose clause order was restored to match the source page image — all extraction-artifact corrections, not edits to legal content. laws.boe.gov.sa has no dedicated lawId page for this bylaw. The two Umm al-Qura Gazette links named in the research brief redirected to the Gazette's current homepage rather than the archived 2022 publication notice, so gazette text itself was not independently re-confirmed this pass. No confirmed amendment to this Implementing Regulation was found since its 14/5/1444H approval: a 2017 CST news item on amending 'the Implementing Regulation of the Telecommunications Law' was checked and found to concern the PRIOR, now-repealed 2001 law's regulation, not this one; a same-titled e-participation consultation page could not be fetched and its lower ID relative to the base law's own 2024 amendment-consultation ID suggests, without full confirmation, that it is the original 2022 pre-approval draft rather than a later amendment round.
